title: Compaction and dream cycle architecture
content: What: The compaction system in src/memory-domain/compaction.js handles cleanup of stale data. It runs pruneDeleted() to soft-delete old entries, then rebuilds the FTS index with rebuildFtsIndex(). The dream cycle additionally targets superseded and stale memories. Why: Without FTS rebuild after pruning, deleted observations remain searchable via FTS until the next manual rebuild. Where: src/memory-domain/compaction.js, called from services/dream.js. Learned: The rebuildFtsIndex function runs `INSERT INTO observations_fts(observations_fts) VALUES('rebuild')` to force FTS re-index. This MUST be called after any bulk deletion. The FTS5 virtual table does NOT auto-sync when underlying content tables change via DELETE — only the content-sync triggers handle row-level changes.

title: Fixed FTS staleness after bulk deletion
content: What: After bulk deletion during compaction, the FTS index was not being rebuilt because the rebuildFtsIndex call was removed in a refactor. Why: The developer assumed SQLite triggers would handle FTS sync, but FTS5 content-sync triggers only handle individual INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, not bulk operations or the `rebuild` command. Where: src/memory-domain/compaction.js. Learned: Always verify FTS index integrity after compaction. The `rebuild` command is the correct way to force a full FTS re-index.

title: Search ranking and FTS interaction
content: What: The search function in src/memory-domain/search.js queries observations_fts for candidate rows, then ranks them with rankObservations(). The FTS query returns rowids that are joined back to the observations table. Why: FTS5 provides the initial candidate set; rankObservations applies the multi-signal ranking. Where: src/memory-domain/search.js. Learned: If the FTS index is stale (missing entries for existing observations), search will not find them even though they exist in the observations table. The FTS index must be kept in sync.
